_source: [8.37] Terrain Effects Chart, Friendly/Enemy Minefield rows + note 13 (PDF p.70); [6.3] Capability Point Expenditure Summary, the seven minefield-entry cells (PDF p.96); rule 26.0 MINEFIELDS (PDF p.38); rule 24.3 CONSTRUCTING MINEFIELD (PDF p.36); [24.17] Construction Chart (PDF p.104); [24.18] Demolition Chart, Real/Fake Minefield rows (PDF p.105). Scan-verified: scratchpad/port/transcriptions/26-minefields-and-24-construction.md, scratchpad/p82_minefields/tec-070.png + constr-104.png, and (the 8.2 review repair) scratchpad/p82_repair/p70-070.png, p96-096.png, p104-104.png, p105-105.png.
_note: Breakdown Points for entering a minefield hexside live in data/breakdown_rates.json (terrain_breakdown_values_8_37.hexside.friendly_minefield=0, .enemy_minefield=2); game.minefields READS them from there rather than duplicating the magnitude here.

entry_cp._comment: 26.21/26.22: CP to enter a minefield hex, ADDED ON TOP of the hex's ordinary terrain entry cost ('+ TEC' in every cell of [6.3]). 'mot_is_full_cpa' models the chart's 'CPA + TEC' cell and rule 26.21's own worked example ('an artillery unit would expend 15 Capability Points to enter an Enemy minefield' -- its entire 15-point CPA).

_entry_cp_source: [6.3] CAPABILITY POINT EXPENDITURE SUMMARY (PDF p.96), read digit-by-digit off a 400dpi render, prints ALL SEVEN cells and is the only place in the book that does: 'Enter a friendly minefield hex: Any unit with an Eng unit 0 + TEC / Non-motorized unit, no Eng unit 1 + TEC / Motorized unit, no Eng unit 4 + TEC. Enter an enemy minefield hex: Non-motorized unit with an Eng unit 2 + TEC / Motorized unit with an Eng unit 4 + TEC / Non-motorized unit, no Eng unit 4 + TEC / Motorized unit, no Eng unit CPA + TEC.' The four unescorted cells agree exactly with [8.37]'s two minefield rows (+1/+4 Friendly, +4/+CPA Enemy).
_settled_escort_discount_was_owner_rulin: SETTLED BY THE BOOK, 2026-07-26 (8.2 review repair) -- this file previously declared an OWNER RULING NEEDED here on the grounds that only 26.24 ('pay only four additional Capability Points to enter an Enemy minefield, rather than their listed cost') and 23.21 ('reduced to six CP's for Motorized units and three CP's for non-motorized units') spoke to the escorted case, and that 'the chart itself is silent'. That was WRONG: only the Terrain Effects Chart had been checked. [6.3] above prints the escorted cells outright -- 2 non-Mot / 4 Mot into an Enemy belt, 0 into a Friendly one -- and reconciles 26.24 (whose flat 4 is the MOTORIZED cell) with the TEC. The engine now implements [6.3] verbatim. 23.21's 6/3 is the outlier: it is the only figure in the book no chart carries, and it is NOT implemented. The engine previously charged a flat 4 for BOTH mobility classes, i.e. it overcharged escorted foot by 2 CP.
_escort_who_source: WHO may escort: [6.3] says 'with an Eng unit'; 23.21 says 'stacked with any Engineer unit (or HQ unit with Engineering capability)'; 26.24/26.25 say narrower -- 'an Engineer battalion or Commonwealth HQs with Engineering capacity' (excluding engineer COMPANIES and Axis HQ-Engineering). ENGINE IMPLEMENTS the [6.3]+23.21 breadth (any general-Engineering unit: EBn, ECoy, HQ-with-Engineering of either side, plus a 23.15 Scorpion battalion at 6+ TOE), because the chart is the arbiter and 23.21 is the numbered Case that describes the escort itself. FLAGGED, not resolved: if the owner prefers 26.24's narrower list, the change is game.minefields.escorts.

scorpion._comment: [23.15] (addition, rulebook Additions & Clarifications -- an addition to Section 23 ENGINEERS, NOT an abstract-game rule; the same appendix block carries [21.11], [24.79], [27.52], [30.36]): 'The Commonwealth Player receives, via the Reinforcement Track, two tank battalions completely refitted with Scorpion tanks (historically the 42nd and 44th Royal Tank Regiments). These two battalions are engineer units but possess ONLY ANTI-MINEFIELD CAPABILITIES. Each battalion is considered to possess engineer unit status while it contains at least six Scorpion TOE Strength Points.' [24.18] Demolition Chart, Real Minefield row: 'Clear | Any E or tank bn with 6+ TOE of Scorpions | 1 Op Stage'. The two counters are already in data/reinforcements_campaign.json (42/44 RTR (Scorpion), model 'scorpion', arrival GT99) and in the [63.0] El Alamein scenarios at 10 TOE each.
scorpion._capabilities: ANTI-MINEFIELD ONLY (23.15 verbatim): clearing a belt (26.13/24.38/[24.18]), escorting a mover through one (26.24 -- the 2/4 discount above), and exempting that mover from the 26.25 destruction roll. NOT construction: a Scorpion battalion may not LAY a minefield ([24.17]'s Build row names EBn/ECoy/CHQ-E) nor build a fortification ([24.17]'s AnyE).

destruction_roll._comment: [26.25]: entering an Enemy minefield NOT escorted by an Engineer/CW-HQ-Engineering, one die per battalion-sized (or less) combat unit and/or per all 2nd/3rd line trucks (collectively). 5 or 6 destroys one TOE Strength Point of tanks/motorized infantry, or one unattached Truck Point.
destruction_roll._dummy_never_destroys: A DUMMY belt rolls NOTHING (fixed 2026-07-26, 8.2 review repair -- the engine had been rolling 26.25 for dummy belts too). 26.11 makes real-vs-dummy THE distinction of rule 26, and 26.23's 'the only difference' clause is scoped to the COST of entry ('the costs to enter a dummy minefield are the same as those for a real minefield'), not to 26.25, which is written about mines physically destroying vehicles. A fake belt that kills tanks would erase the whole bluff mechanic and make the 3-Store dummy strictly better value than the 15+15 real one.
destruction_roll._deferred: 26.25's TRUCK half -- 'one die for all 2nd and 3rd line trucks' collectively, destroying 'one unattached Truck Point' -- and its 'battalion-sized (or less)' size restriction are NOT implemented: the engine rolls one die per moving combat unit regardless of counter size and never rolls for a truck column. Flagged, not silently assumed.

combat_shift._comment: 26.26 + [8.37] note 13. The shift belongs to the DEFENDER and turns on the belt being the DEFENDER'S OWN. [8.37]'s Combat Adjustment columns are read from the non-Phasing side: Friendly Minefield row = -/L1/L1 (Barrage/Anti-Armor/Close Assault), Enemy Minefield row = -/-/- . Note 13: 'If ASSAULTING forces are in an Enemy minefield, the non-Phasing forces receive L1 shifts for Anti-Armor and Close Assault if not already receiving them for occupying a Friendly minefield.' 26.26 says the same twice over: 'On any anti-tank or close assault combat in which the attacking units are in an Enemy minefield OR in which there is a Close Assault against an Enemy unit in an Enemy Minefield, the defending Player adjusts all columns one in his favor.' So: the defender gets ONE column (never two) if a belt HE laid stands either on the hex being assaulted or on any hex the assault comes from; a belt the ATTACKER laid grants nothing. Not applicable to Barrage (26.26: 'does not apply to artillery bombardment'; both TEC rows print '-' under Barrage).
combat_shift._ownership_fix: Fixed 2026-07-26 (8.2 review repair): the engine had keyed both shifts on 'is there ANY belt on the target hex', which over-granted (a belt the attacker laid, i.e. the chart's Enemy Minefield row, whose AA/CA cells are '-') and under-granted (note 13's actual case -- assaulting forces standing in the defender's belt -- was never checked at all, because only the target hex was read).

construction._comment: 24.3 CONSTRUCTING MINEFIELDS. Costs and Op-Stage count read off both the rule prose (24.33/24.34/24.32) and the Construction Chart (24.17), which agree on everything except the terrain list.
construction._owner_ruling_2_terrain: [24.35] (prose, verbatim): 'Minefields may be constructed in clear, sand/gravel, or rough hexes.' [24.17] Construction Chart, Real AND Fake Minefield rows (verbatim): 'May only be built in Clear, Sand/Gravel and Salt Marsh hexes.' Rough vs Salt Marsh -- not a plausible OCR slip either way, both scan-verified at 300dpi/200dpi on two independent renders. ENGINE IMPLEMENTS 24.35's LIST (terrain_allowed above: Clear/Gravel/Rough) because it is the numbered rule's own prose, not a chart's compressed restatement -- OWNER RULING NEEDED to confirm or override with Salt Marsh in place of Rough.
construction._builder_units: [24.31] (prose): 'Minefields may be constructed by any Engineering unit (or Commonwealth HQ Engineers).' [24.17] Build row: 'EBn, ECoy or CHQ-E' (key: CHQ-E = ALLIED headquarters with engineering capability). Prose and chart AGREE, and both are NARROWER than the fortification row's AnyE (= 'any engineer battalion, engineer company, or headquarters unit with engineering capability', either side): an AXIS HQ with engineering capability may build a fortification but may NOT lay a minefield. The engine implements exactly this split (game.construction.lays_minefield vs .builds_engineering) using Unit.engineer's three general values -- 'ENGINEER' (EBn/ECoy) and 'HQ_ENGINEER' (23.14's HQ with an E beside its Stacking Points), plus 'SCORPION' which builds nothing.

fortification._comment: 24.4 CONSTRUCTING FORTIFICATIONS. One Level per project; 24.48 caps a major city at its printed Level (2, or 3 for Alexandria/Cairo) and a field fortification at Level 2 (Level 1 then Level 2 -- the chart's own counter set, 'represented by counters as being either Level 1 or Level 2', 24.41).
fortification._owner_ruling_3_fortification_terrain: PROSE-VS-CHART COLLISION, flagged 2026-07-26 (8.2 review repair) -- the same shape as ruling #2 above, and previously silent. [24.44] (prose, verbatim): 'Construction of new fortifications may take place in any hex except MOUNTAIN, SALT MARSH, DESERT, MAJOR CITY, and DELTA.' [24.17] Construction Chart, 1 Level of Fortification row, Restrictions cell (verbatim, scan p.104): 'May not be built in a Salt Marsh, Delta or Major City hex' -- three of the five, no Mountain and no Desert. ENGINE IMPLEMENTS 24.44's FULL LIST (terrain_excluded above), consistently with ruling #2's precedent: the numbered rule's own prose over the chart's compressed restatement. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: this is the STRICTER reading and it bars fortifying DESERT hexes -- i.e. the southern (desert) flank of the Alamein line. That consequence is recorded here so the ruling is made on the book's wording and not on a balance argument; per port rule 1 the engine will not adopt the looser list merely because the looser list would fortify Alamein.
fortification._owner_ruling_3b_rebuild_in_zoc: Same collision, second cell: [24.45] (prose) permits rebuilding a destroyed Level in an Enemy ZOC generally ('the rebuilding (or repairing) of fortifications may take place in an Enemy Zone of Control'); the chart's Restrictions cell says only 'May be rebuilt in a MAJOR CITY hex in an enemy ZOC'. ENGINE IMPLEMENTS 24.45's general permission (game.construction.fort_buildable's is_rebuild branch). Flagged, lower confidence.
fortification._owner_ruling_4_concurrent_construction: [24.46] (prose, verbatim): 'No other construction -- of any type -- may take place in a hex which is undergoing fortification construction.' The Construction Chart's Fortification row Restrictions cell ends '...No construction other than construction/demolition of ports and/or flying boat facilities may simultaneously occur in same hex,' which reads as a carve-out 24.46 does not mention. ENGINE IMPLEMENTS 24.46's FLAT PROHIBITION -- game.construction.hex_construction_conflict, both directions (a banked FORT bars any other project on the hex; any other banked project bars a new FORT). No port or flying-boat construction exists in this engine, so the chart's carve-out has no subject regardless. (Until 2026-07-26 this key CLAIMED the prohibition was implemented when nothing enforced it -- a FORT and a REAL_MINEFIELD could run concurrently on one hex. Fixed in the 8.2 review repair.)

_owner_ruling_5_dump_costs_not_in_scope: Found incidentally while re-reading [24.17] for this file: the Construction Chart's Real/Fake Supply Dump rows read 10 Stores / 2 CP's, while rule 24.9 (which game/construction.py's DUMP_STORES=20/DUMP_CP=3 already implements, pre-dating this task) reads 20 Store Points / 3 CP real, 3 CP dummy (no stores). [6.3] (p.96) prints a third figure for the CP half: 'Construct a Real or Dummy/Non-Dump Supply Dump 3/2'. Two of three numbers disagree. Outside this file's scope (rule 26 / 24.3 / 24.4) -- NOT changed here, flagged for whoever picks it up.
_confirms_zero_cp_construction: [6.3] (p.96): 'Construction/Demolition of items other than Supply Dumps ... 0' -- the engine's construction beat charges no Capability Points for a minefield, a fortification or a railroad hex, and this is why. What construction costs a unit is its whole Operations Stage (24.0/24.12: 'units involved in construction may not expend any Capability Points'), which the engine models by booking the unit out of movement.
